obligations.evidence: Field allow-lists; chunk limits; context budget
obligations.gate: Context contains only necessary and authorized data
obligations.name: Data minimization
obligations.text: Expose only the minimum fields, chunks, conversation history and user attributes required for the current task.

obligations.gate: All indexed objects have verifiable provenance
obligations.name: Provenance and integrity
obligations.text: Record source identity, owner, classification, timestamp, checksum, version, approval status and transformation lineage for every indexed object.

obligations.evidence: Service accounts; workload identity; role inventory
obligations.gate: No shared runtime or administrator credentials
obligations.name: Workload identities
obligations.text: Use separate identities for users, agents, ingestion, retrieval, administration, migrations and monitoring.

obligations.evidence: GRANT review; role tests; privilege reports
obligations.gate: Application identities have only required privileges
obligations.name: Least privilege
obligations.text: Runtime agents must not own objects, create roles, alter schemas, bypass RLS or access unrestricted administration. Retrieval roles should be read-only.

obligations.evidence: Vault integration; rotation logs; certificate policy
obligations.gate: No static credentials in code, prompts or configuration files
obligations.name: Credential security
obligations.text: Prefer short-lived credentials, workload identity or certificate authentication. Store unavoidable secrets in a vault and rotate automatically.

obligations.gate: Databases are not publicly reachable
obligations.name: Private network access
obligations.text: Restrict databases to approved workloads using private connectivity, firewall rules, service endpoints and workload-level policies.

obligations.gate: Only approved sources can enter production indexes
obligations.name: Approved sources and connectors
obligations.text: Allow-list repositories, file types, connectors and content owners. Treat internal and external content as untrusted.

obligations.gate: Unsafe objects are quarantined before indexing
obligations.name: Content scanning
obligations.text: Scan documents for malware, embedded objects, scripts, macros, suspicious URLs, hidden text and adversarial instructions.

obligations.gate: Unapproved content cannot be retrieved in production
obligations.name: Quarantine and approval
obligations.text: Quarantine new or materially changed content until automated controls and, for sensitive collections, human approval complete.

obligations.gate: Source changes propagate within defined SLA
obligations.name: Change and revocation handling
obligations.text: Delete or rebuild indexed content when a source is deleted, reclassified, expired or loses approval.

obligations.evidence: Pre-filter query; authorization logs; negative tests
obligations.gate: Authorization occurs before and after retrieval
obligations.name: Permission-aware retrieval
obligations.text: Authenticate the requester, resolve current entitlements, filter eligible content before semantic search and revalidate before sending chunks to the model.

obligations.gate: Oversized or policy-conflicting context is rejected
obligations.name: Context constraints
obligations.text: Apply chunk-count, token, sensitivity, classification and result-size limits. Use default-deny behavior on missing or conflicting metadata.

obligations.gate: Material responses are traceable to approved sources
obligations.name: Source attribution
obligations.text: Attach immutable source identifiers and provenance to retrieved content and material responses.

obligations.evidence: Prompt boundaries; policy layer; adversarial tests
obligations.gate: Retrieved instructions cannot override control-plane policy
obligations.name: Prompt-injection containment
obligations.text: Separate system instructions, user input, retrieved data, tool output and memory. Mark retrieved content as data, not executable instruction.

obligations.gate: No secrets are exposed to the model or logs
obligations.name: Secret exclusion
obligations.text: Never place credentials, tokens, connection strings, private keys, privileged schemas or sensitive hidden policies into model context.

obligations.evidence: Agent registry; identity mapping; owner attestation
obligations.gate: Every production agent is registered and attributable
obligations.name: Unique identity and purpose
obligations.text: Assign each agent a unique workload identity, approved purpose, explicit data boundary and accountable owner.

obligations.gate: Only approved, narrowly scoped tools are callable
obligations.name: Tool allow-listing
obligations.text: Expose narrow business functions rather than unrestricted SQL, shell, HTTP, file or API tools. Remove unused tools.

obligations.gate: Limits prevent uncontrolled execution and consumption
obligations.name: Least agency
obligations.text: Constrain functionality, permissions and autonomy. Define maximum task duration, steps, spend, records affected and data volume.

obligations.gate: High-risk actions cannot execute autonomously
obligations.name: Human approval
obligations.text: Require approval for sensitive disclosure, external communication, entitlement changes, material writes/deletes, high-impact decisions and bulk exports.

obligations.evidence: Tenant keys; memory ACLs; validation pipeline
obligations.gate: One user or tenant cannot access another’s memory
obligations.name: Memory isolation
obligations.text: Separate short-term context from persistent memory; bind memory to tenant and subject; validate before reuse.

obligations.evidence: mTLS or signed messages; schema validation
obligations.gate: Peer identity and message integrity are verified
obligations.name: Inter-agent trust
obligations.text: Treat agent-to-agent messages, shared memory and tool responses as untrusted; authenticate peers and validate message schemas.

obligations.gate: Free-text model output never executes directly
obligations.name: Deterministic output validation
obligations.text: Validate SQL, API parameters, file paths, URLs and structured output before execution by downstream systems.

obligations.evidence: Central audit trail; access controls; retention
obligations.gate: Material activity is reconstructable without logging excessive data
obligations.name: Tamper-resistant audit logging
obligations.text: Log identity, agent/model/policy version, source IDs, authorization decision, tools, affected records, approvals and policy actions, while redacting secrets.

obligations.evidence: Test evidence; threat model; red-team report
obligations.gate: No critical findings remain open at production release
obligations.name: Security testing and release gates
obligations.text: Perform threat modeling, authorization testing, prompt-injection tests, poisoning tests, agent red teaming and regression testing before release and material change.

obligations.gate: Agent can be contained and stopped promptly
obligations.name: Resilience and shutdown
obligations.text: Implement rate limits, loop controls, budget limits, circuit breakers, rollback, agent revocation and an emergency kill switch.

residual_risk.body: No control in this catalogue prevents a decision that breaks no rule and is nonetheless wrong — auto-closing a real incident, or recording an unimplemented control as implemented. Nothing leaves, no allowlist breaks, and the difference between the harmful action and the correct one is only whether the reasoning was sound. The compensating controls are the decision record, which makes the reasoning reviewable, and sampling review of automated dispositions, which is why that review is a security control rather than quality assurance.
residual_risk.title: Residual risk: a steered but permitted decision
